sentences.text: 5. The present petition has been filed by the petitioner on the grounds and it has been argued by his counsel that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the aforementioned case.
The petitioner was granted concession ncession of anticipatory bail and was regularly appearing before the learned trial Court.

However, on 22.10.2024, he could not appear before the Court due to medical reasons and some miscommunication with his counsel resulting into cancellation of his bail and ultimately declaring him as a proclaimed offender..
It is further submitted that the petitioner had been declared a proclaimed offender without following the proper procedure prescribed under Section 82 of Cr.P.C.

Even otherwise, the matter stands amic amicably ably settled between the petitioner and respondent No. 2/complainant and in pursuance of the same, the petitioner had paid the entire disputed amount to respondent No. 2 and the petitioner will shortly file a petition before this Court seeking quashing of the FIR in question on the basis of the said compromise.
Hence, it is urged that the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

6. Learned State counsel has argued tha thatt there is no infirmity or illegality in the impugned order as the petitioner had intentionally avoided his 2 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:035567 CRM-M-9690 9690-2025 (O&M) -3- appearance before the learned trial Court.
Hence, it is urged that the petition is liable to be dismissed.

7. On the other hand, learned counsel ffor or respondent No. 2/complainant has admitted the factum of compromise having arrived at between the parties and also that the entire disputed amount has been paid to him by the petitione.
petitione.
He has also submitted that he has no ob objection jection if the present petition is allowed and the impugned order is quashed in favour of the petitioner.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties at considerable length and have also gone through the material placed on record.

9. On giving due deliberations to the contentions as raised by learned counsel for the parties and on an overall perusal of the orders passed by the learned trial Court from the date of initiating proceedings under Section 82 of Cr.P.C. as against the petitioner petitioner till the date of declaring him a proclaimed offender,, I am of the considered opinion that the impugned order dated 13.01.2025 suffers from material illegalities and is liable to be quashed with all the consequential proceedings arising therefrom.

sentences.text: After going through the material placed on reco record rd as well as the copies of zimni zim orders passed by the learned trial Court, it is revealed that on 02.12.2024 since the non-bailable 02.12.2024, bailable warrants issued against the petitioner were received back unserved, the learned trial Court had ordered for issuance of proclamation against him for 13.01.2025..

A bare perusal of this order shows that the learned trial Court before ordering for publication of proclamation has not recorded its proper satisfaction that that the petitioner had absconded or was concealing himself so t h a t t h e w a r r a n t o f a r r e s t , p r e v i o u s l y i s s u e d , c a n n o t 3 o f 5 N e u t r a l C i t a t i o n No:=2025:PHHC:035567 CRM-M-9690 9690-2025 (O&M) -4- be executed, despite reasonable diligence, which was in violation of the provisions of Section 82(1) of Cr.P.C.

Reliance in this regard can be placed upon Rohit Kumar Vs. State of Delhi : 2008 Crl. J. 2561.
11.

sentences.text: Further, a perusal of the statement of the serving police official ASI Charan Singh reveals that the proclamation was not read over in some conspicuous place of the town or village in which the petitionerr was supposed to be residing.

As per Section 82 (2) of Cr.P.C. ffor publication, the proclamation has to be first publicly read in some conspicuous place of the town or village in which the accused ordinarily resides; then the same has to be affixed to some conspicuous part of the house or homestead in which the accused ordinarily resides or to some conspicuous place of such town or village and thereafter a copy of the proclamation has to be affixed to some conspicuous part of the Court-house.
house.

The three sub sub-clauses (a)-(c)
(c) in Section 82 (2)(i) of the Cr.P.C. are conjunctive and not disjunctive, which means that there would be no valid publication of the proclamation unless all the three modes of publication are proved.

Reliance in this regard can be placed upon Pawan Kumar Gupta Vs. The State of W.B. : 1973 CriLJ 1368.
12.
